title: Midwife
description: Midwives focuses on a “well model” rather than a “sick model” of healthcare. They support women and their families during preconception, through pregnancy and postpartum. In addition to promote, protect and sustain breastfeeding. They work in a variety of settings, including hospitals and both private and government facilities, home and clinic. They are part of a multidisciplinary team that includes but not limited to physicians, dietitians and nurses. • The position holders have a wide range of duties under the scope of the midwife, that include assessment, screening clinical examinations, health education, counseling and identifying any deviation from normal. They assess, implement and evaluate programs of care in antenatal, postnatal period, preconception for women at reproductive age and their newborn/babies. Ensuring consistency of approach, applying current best evidence based, high quality health advice and support. Provides skilled, safe, holistic, culturally competent, and person-centered midwifery care to the woman, her family and community in collaboration with the multidisciplinary team irrespective of healthcare setting. • Provide peri-conceptional care antenatal, postpartum care, newborn care, family planning, parenthood and educational programs. • Practice in accordance with agreed policies and procedures that guide midwifery practice (Adheres to and implements policies and procedures). • Cooperate and liaise with multi-disciplinary team (work as part of a team of healthcare professionals) to provide the best care and guidance to women, newborn, children, and their families. • To detect any deviation from normality and seek medical advice and ensure appropriate referrals are made to hospitals by physician for ongoing care for low and high-risk pregnancies. • Provides guidance for and supervision of personnel accountable to the Graduate Registered midwives. • Keep up to date with midwifery practice by undertaking relevant continuing professional development. • Acknowledges her own limitations in knowledge, judgment and/or skills, and functions within those limitations. • Demonstrate a sense of teamwork and effective communication. • Checks the health of the mother and baby, assesses the full range of care needs for pregnancy, develops, implements and evaluates the plan of care for the mother through the antenatal period. She provides useful information to help her have a healthy pregnancy, including advice about healthy eating and exercise throughout the Antenatal phase. • Provides comprehensive postnatal care, support the mother in making the transition as easy as possible. • Early detection of any complications and promptly escalates to appropriate physician. • Nutritional guidance. • Guidance on breastfeeding. • Contraception and family planning guidance. • Maintains contemporaneous record keeping of care given to women, newborn or infant based on available policy/ guidance. • Co-ordinate health education programs under the direction, consultation and guidance from nursing Operations and collaboration with the women health and child and adolescent health team at PHC. • Educating women as well as their partners and family members and provide health counselling and support for them during various stages of reproductive • cycle including antenatal, intrapartum, postnatal, breastfeeding, preconception, and family planning. • Education can be on individual basis and in groups. • Educate women and family members regarding aspects of newborn, infant and • young childcare, including importance of breastfeeding, options for infant feeding, baby safety, basics of childcare, developmental stages, vaccinations, weaning, exercise and any other related information. • Signposting and raising awareness for all aspects of woman and neonate/infant health screening activities in Qatar. • Ensure client confidentiality is always upheld. Appropriate use of professional and confidential methods of internal and external referral to another health care team member as necessary. • Ensure that all Midwifery related health promotion activities are widely understood and advocated by individuals and communities to ensure far reaching benefits and positive outcomes for our current and future generations. • Performs and documents a comprehensive medical, obstetrics and gynecology history, physical, psychosocial, emotional, ethnic, cultural, and spiritual assessment of the women’s health status. • Undertakes antenatal bookings (open file). • Examining and monitoring pregnant and postpartum women. • Assessment and evaluation of newborn (by inspection) • Assessing care requirements and writing care plans. • Carrying out screening tests. • Providing information, emotional support and reassurance to women and their families. • Place orders for Laboratory work as required, taking patient samples, take vital sign and required measurement for mother and newborn. According to the PHCC policies. • Advising and supporting parents in the daily care of their newborn babies • Identifying high-risk pregnancies. • Provide emotional support and guidance during events such as miscarriage, termination, stillbirth, neonatal abnormality, and neonatal death. (Where appropriately trained). • Detect any deviation from normality and seek medical advice. To ensure appropriate and timely internal referrals are made. • Identify high risk pregnancies and make internal referrals to doctors and other medical specialists as needed. • Complete the postnatal referral order (internal and external referral), direct booking for 6 weeks check by physician and postnatal continuity of care. (According to the PHCC policies.) • Should an emergency delivery occur at a Health Center; provide suitable care to mother in labor, and newborn if delivered in line with PHCC policy. • Ensure infection control measures are followed. • Process of transferring mother & her delivered baby to secondary care facility. • Full documentation carried out Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Midwifery. OR bachelor’s degree in nursing and recognized post-graduate diploma in Midwifery. • Must be registered DHP License (or eligible to register) as a midwife in the state of Qatar. • ALSO, BLS, NRP course • At least 5 years’ experience working within a Maternity setting (experience in all maternity settings are desirable, however Antenatal and postnatal care experience is essential), Neonatal/Pediatric experience is an added advantage. • Ability to maintain quality, safety, and/or infection control standards. Using standard precautions, infection prevention and control strategies, and clean technique. • Knowledge of related accreditation and certification requirements. • Knowledge of midwifery theory, procedure, and standards. • Ability to develop, assess, evaluate, and implement individual women and child health programs of care (effective care). • Ability to keep up to date with the latest developments in the profession so that their skills and knowledge remain current. • Knowledge and/or understanding of human rights culture, beliefs and traditional health practices. • Behaves in a courteous, non-judgmental, non-discriminatory, and culturally appropriate manner with all clients. • Able to maintain the confidentiality of all information shared by the woman; communicates essential information between/among other health providers or family members only with explicit permission from the woman and compelling need

title: Allied Health Technologist
description: The incumbent has the responsibility to Evaluate, plan, direct and administer the physical therapy modalities of treatment as prescribed by a licensed physician. To administers treatments and physical agents as prescribed by a referring physician in an effort to restore function and prevent disability following injury, disease or physical disability. And to assists patients to reach their maximum performance and level of functioning, while learning to live within the limits of their capabilities. Demonstrates knowledge of physical therapy modalities. • Perform treatment techniques to improve patient mobility, including breathing and relaxation techniques, therapeutic exercise, manual therapy and soft tissue techniques, electrotherapy modalities. Gait training, pain management, cold/heat therapy. • Ability to perform appropriate assessment on all patients related to the therapy requested and provided and reassessments. This includes adolescent, geriatric patients and the general patient population. • Assess, evaluate, diagnose and plan an individualized exercise program as well as provide education to enable the patient to self-manage their condition. These include breathing and cough techniques to manage COPD and falls prevention programs for patients at high risk. • Provide treatments for conditions such as Musculoskeletal conditions, geriatric conditions, women’s health issues, chronic conditions and facial palsy. • Provide assessment, education as well as self-management programs to support patients with obesity, diabetes, arthritis and other chronic diseases. • Treats patients and their families with respect and dignity. Identifies and addresses psychosocial, cultural, ethnic and religious/spiritual needs of patients and family. • Provide patients with treatments including, manual therapy, therapeutic physical exercises and the application of electro-physical modalities. • Develop treatment plans according to patient’s individual needs, history profile, and symptoms. • Provide consultation sessions on physical health improvement, in accordance with regulatory requirements, and credentialing requirements. • Follow-up on patient’s progress and response to exercise programs, to identify needed program change.Coordinates delegates and supervises responsibilities assigned to supportive staff and participate in operational aspects of the department, maintains performance improvement activities within the department and participates in Quality assurance activities. • Ensures that patient changes are accurate and entered on a timely basis. Participates in all infection control, departmental equipment training, organizational safety and fire safety programs. Requirements: Bachelor of Science in Physiotherapy or equivalent. • Licensed to practice Physiotherapy at point of hire • DHP License • CPR course certificate. • Minimum 1 year of internship/training in a hospital or equivalent. • Minimum 3 years of experience in physiotherapy
